/start: Checks that your Persona, World Info, and System Prompt are all turned on. If they are, it sends and stores the character's opening message. If not, it shows you what's off and how to fix it. You can also just type "start" as a plain message to get the greeting regardless.
/help: Opens this guide. Pick a category, then tap a command to see what it does and what it changes.
/cancel: Cancels the current scoped input step, such as session naming, memory input, image prompts, settings, or other panel-driven text entry. Nothing is applied; the pending input is cleared safely.
/status: Shows a formatted read-only session status message directly in Telegram.
/new: Creates a fresh isolated session. It asks for a name first (1–80 characters), then switches you to it. Send /cancel if you change your mind — no empty session is left behind.
/reset: Opens a confirmation panel first. When you confirm, it clears the conversation, deletes only that session's Hindsight documents, and wipes its variants and summary. Other sessions are untouched. The session stays available but empty — it won't send the character greeting afterward. Type "start" if you want the opening message.
/session: Lets you switch between sessions, create new ones, or delete inactive ones. Deleting a session removes its SQLite data and session-scoped Hindsight documents, but only if Hindsight cleanup succeeds — if it can't verify cleanup, it keeps the session rather than leaving orphaned memories. Active or busy sessions can't be deleted.
/sync: Opens Live API Sync for this session. It talks to SillyTavern's local API — no chat files or JSONL transfers. Toggle realtime to do an initial reconciliation before turning on background sync. Sync now runs a one-shot API reconciliation even when background realtime is off; Refresh status only redraws state. If there's a sync-ID mismatch, initial divergence, two-sided edits, or oversized API records, sync stops instead of guessing. Credentials stay separate from Telegram.
/update: Checks a stable GitHub release and binds confirmation to the displayed version. Installation requires a clean main checkout, an SSH-signed annotated tag trusted by an independently installed allowed-signers file, and a safe managed live mirror. It verifies and stages before activation. Changed runtime dependencies require manual installation. Restart failures are reported explicitly; session data and private configuration are not copied or reset.
/providers: Opens the provider and model catalog. Choose Story or Utility first, then pick a provider and model. Story handles character replies; Utility handles summaries, memory, and other bridge tasks. Supported OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic Messages, and OpenCode Muse transports can generate; catalog-only entries are view-only. Provider health and Refresh models are available as buttons in the provider list, after choosing Story or Utility.
/character: Opens the character panel — each card is shown as rank | character | action. Rank S/A/B/C/D appears only in this main menu; Character Info and Optimizer pickers show names only. Character Info shows the PNG preview. Optimizer offers Auto Optimize or Manual Suggestion; Manual Suggestion shows the current editable values first and later suggestions revise the temporary preview instead of restarting from the installed card. Apply reranks the installed card. Refresh reloads native card labels and treats an unchanged redraw as success.
/persona: Opens native SillyTavern Persona controls. Choose, create, edit, or disable a Persona — all stored in settings.json and the native User Avatars folder. The review panel shows the description in Telegram's copyable code block. Delete only targets inactive, unreferenced Personas — the active one and any used by other sessions are protected.
/world: Opens World Info selection. You can activate multiple JSON lorebooks at the same time — they're validated and merged at prompt time. Use Upload World JSON to add a native World Info file, or the trash button to delete an inactive file. Active or referenced files are protected.
/note: Opens the Author's Note panel. Off clears it. User input waits for your next scoped text message and uses it as the note.
/systemprompt: Opens the native JSON/TXT System Prompt picker. The prompt body stays private — it's applied during generation, but menus and /status only show the label.
/language: Opens per-session reply language controls. Auto follows whatever language you're writing in. A fixed language adds a final render pass to every response so it comes out in that language — streaming preview is disabled in fixed mode so you only see the final output.
/language <language>: Sets the active session response language directly. Use auto to follow the user language, or a supported fixed language value. Invalid values are rejected without changing the session.
/expression: Opens character expression controls for this session. Automatic mode reads the model's reply, classifies the emotion locally, and sends a native sprite only when the expression actually changes. Manual mode lets you pick a sprite directly. If no matching sprite exists, it falls back to neutral, then the avatar, then text-only.
/imagine: Opens prompt input for image generation — but only when you've explicitly configured an image provider. Enter 1–4,000 characters, or use /imagine <prompt> directly. Unconfigured or unsupported providers fail closed. /cancel aborts.
/imagine <prompt>: Runs image generation immediately with the supplied 1–4,000 character prompt when an image provider is configured. Unsupported or unconfigured image providers fail closed.
/settings: Opens generation settings for this session. Pick reasoning or edit temperature, max tokens, top P, frequency penalty, presence penalty, or stop sequences. Humanizer is one ON/OFF toggle; it is off by default.
/stream: Opens the streaming on/off panel for this chat. Choose a button to apply the state. Typed forms such as /stream on and /stream off are accepted for compatibility with the command router but deliberately open the same panel rather than silently changing state. Token-limit auto-continuation stays cumulative, cancellable, and bounded.
/preset: Opens preset controls. Apply, save, or delete validated generation setting presets — all from the panel.
/macro: Opens a panel, then waits for one text message to preview supported SillyTavern macros. Send /cancel to leave without running anything.
/macro <text>: Expands supported SillyTavern macros immediately against the supplied text and returns the preview without changing the transcript.
/stscript: Opens the allowlisted STscript panel. Only safe bridge actions are exposed — no shell commands, no filesystem access, no network requests. Reset goes through the normal session confirmation flow.
/regen: Generates a fresh response variant for your latest user turn. The previous variant is kept — use /swipe to browse them.
/swipe: Opens stored response variants for the latest turn. Browse through them and keep the one you like best.
/branch: Opens the response branch selector for the active session.
/continue: Continues the latest assistant response from where it left off. When a streaming provider hits its output token limit, the bridge can automatically continue with up to three bounded continuation requests while keeping the live preview cumulative; use /continue when you deliberately want another segment after that.
/edit: Opens a panel, then waits for replacement text for your latest user message. Send /cancel to leave it unchanged. The response is regenerated from the edited text.
/edit <text>: Replaces the latest user turn immediately with the supplied text and regenerates the assistant response. The operation uses the same session-scoped edit/recovery path as the panel form.
/retry: Retries the latest failed character response. It replays the original message without creating a duplicate committed turn — clean recovery after a crash or timeout.
/prompt: Opens a read-only prompt inspector with sections for budget, memory/RAG, and group context. Use /prompt text for the full plain diagnostic output.
/prompt text: Sends the full plain-text safe prompt diagnostic output directly instead of opening the prompt-inspector panel. It reports diagnostics without exposing provider credentials.
/memory: Opens Hindsight memory controls. You can turn memory on or off and search within the active session. Recall is always session-scoped — it never pulls in memories from other sessions, users, or characters.
/memory search <query>: Searches Hindsight memory for <query> within the active session and returns up to five matching remembered facts. Recall stays strictly session-scoped, so results never come from another session.
/memory curated: Opens the curated-memory panel to view durable distilled facts or refresh them with the utility model. Memory must be enabled for refresh.
/memory curated refresh: Refreshes curated durable memory immediately with the configured Utility model. Hindsight memory must be enabled. The curated facts remain scoped to the active session and do not replace the transcript.
/remember: Opens a panel, then waits for one explicit long-term fact to store in Hindsight. Send /cancel to leave without storing anything.
/remember <fact>: Stores one explicit fact immediately in active-session Hindsight memory. The fact is bounded and session-scoped; it is never written to another session.
/summarize: Opens a confirmation panel before regenerating the active-session summary from its stored conversation and current memory context. The resulting summary remains scoped to this session and is used as continuity context when older turns are compacted.
/databank: Opens Data Bank RAG controls — check status, list documents, search, remove, or reindex. Uploading different content with the same filename creates a new active version while keeping older versions out of retrieval. Use /databank versions <filename> to inspect history and /databank activate <filename> <version> to roll back atomically.
/databank search <query>: Searches the active Data Bank document versions for matching chunks and returns bounded results. Inactive historical versions stay out of retrieval.
/databank versions <filename>: Lists stored versions for one Data Bank filename, including the active version and chunk/byte counts.
/databank activate <filename> <version>: Atomically switches retrieval to the requested stored version of a Data Bank filename. Use a numeric version, optionally prefixed with v.
/databank reindex [filename]: Rebuilds embeddings for the current embedding namespace. With no filename it reindexes active Data Bank documents; with a filename it limits the operation to that document.
/databank remove <filename> confirm: Deletes every stored version of one Data Bank filename only when the final confirm token is present. Without confirm, the bridge returns the exact confirmation command instead of deleting anything.
/voice: Opens automatic quote-driven TTS controls. Use the panel buttons to turn it on or off. When enabled, dialogue in straight double quotes can be synthesized from both user and character messages; narration and unquoted text stay silent. Typed /voice on or /voice off also opens the panel rather than changing state silently.
/voice_input: Opens voice-input transcription controls for enablement, STT model, and language. Use the panel to apply changes; typed on/off/status/model forms route to the same controls.
/voice_input language: Opens the STT language panel. Auto detects from the audio, a fixed code forces one language, and User input asks you each time.
/group: Only works inside a Telegram Forum Topic. Opens topic-local group controls — New group session asks for a name, then walks you through picking characters and World Info. Director mode makes one hidden bounded model call per normal user turn to choose a known speaker and a short pacing/scene direction; that decision is never stored in the transcript and falls back to round-robin if it fails.
/group status: Shows whether the Forum Topic group is enabled, its turn mode, members, and current or forced speaker. /group list is an equivalent status alias.
/group add <character>: Adds a resolved native character card to the current Forum Topic group. The default session character is included when the first additional member is added, and groups are capped at six characters.
/group remove <character>: Removes an existing character from the current Forum Topic group. If fewer than two members remain, group generation is disabled automatically.
/group speak <character>: Forces one existing group member to take the next character turn. The character must already belong to the group.
/group mode <mode>: Sets the Forum Topic group turn mode to round_robin, contextual, director, manual, or autonomous. Leaving manual mode also clears manual turn ownership.
/group on|off: Enables or disables the configured Forum Topic group directly. Enabling requires at least two members; disabling falls back to the session default character.
/group next: Advances the stored group turn index to the next configured member. The group must contain at least two characters.
/group goal: Shows the current hidden Director objective for this Forum Topic group. The objective is session-local, capped at 1,200 characters, and never added to the roleplay transcript.
/group goal <objective>: Sets or replaces the hidden Director objective for the active group session. It guides speaker selection and scene direction without being revealed to the characters; use /group goal clear to remove it.
/group goal clear: Clears the active group session hidden Director objective. It does not alter the roleplay transcript or structured scene state.
/scene: Shows the active session's structured scene state — bounded continuity such as location, weather, participants, and known facts — without displaying the full transcript.
/scene refresh: Rebuilds structured scene state with the configured utility model. It runs as optional background continuity work and never replaces the original conversation history. Use /scene clear to remove it.
/scene clear: Clears only the active session's stored structured scene state. It does not delete or rewrite the conversation transcript, session summary, Hindsight memory, or Data Bank content.
